lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach Araceae with two project doors: conspicuous spathe/spadix aroids and the highly reduced duckweed lineage now included in modern Araceae.

project_scope.selection_mode: Project module across Amorphophallus, Arisaema, Pistia, Lemna, Spirodela and Wolffia
project_scope.note: Modern Kew classification places Lemna, Spirodela and Wolffia in Araceae. Flora of North America treats the duckweeds in the older family Lemnaceae, but its root/frond keys remain useful morphologically.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: First decide which Araceae door you have. A conventional aroid has many tiny flowers crowded on a fleshy spadix, usually subtended by a spathe. A duckweed is a tiny floating frond with the same lineage reduced almost beyond recognition.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Extremely broad in the project pool: tuberous terrestrial herbs, floating rosettes, and millimeter-scale free-floating fronds. Conventional aroids often have sheathing leaf bases; duckweeds replace normal shoots and leaves with frond-like bodies.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: The classic family architecture is a spadix of minute flowers associated with a spathe. Flowers may be bisexual or unisexual and perianth may be absent. In duckweeds the inflorescence is drastically reduced and seldom seen.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Variable; not a good first family-level field character in this project.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Do not make 'big heart-shaped leaf' the family rule. Learn spathe + spadix for ordinary aroids, then separately learn the duckweed root-count door.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: two-door family overview → spathe/spadix → terrestrial/floating aroid doors → duckweed root-count card → taxonomy reconciliation
visual_lesson.intro: Araceae is one of the best evolutionary visual lessons in the project: titan arum and a speck of watermeal are relatives. The family makes sense once the learner sees normal aroid architecture and then the extreme reduction of duckweeds.

steps.title: 1 · Learn the spathe and spadix
steps.look_for: Many tiny flowers packed on a fleshy spadix, with a modified bract—the spathe—beside or around it.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the core reproductive architecture of ordinary aroids.

steps.title: 2 · Arisaema door
steps.look_for: Pedately divided leaf with several leaflets and a green spathe surrounding a spadix whose slender appendage projects well beyond it.
steps.why_it_matters: Provides the best project native-style terrestrial aroid anchor.

steps.title: 3 · Amorphophallus door
steps.photo_role: titan arum inflorescence + giant divided leaf
steps.look_for: Massive tuber-derived plant with an enormous spathe/spadix inflorescence and a single giant repeatedly divided leaf.
steps.why_it_matters: Memorable comparison showing how large conventional aroid architecture can become.

steps.title: 4 · Pistia door
steps.look_for: Floating rosette of velvety, ribbed, spongy leaves with long hanging roots; tiny spathe/spadix tucked near the leaf base.
steps.why_it_matters: Bridges ordinary aroids and the free-floating duckweed habit.

steps.title: 5 · Duckweed triad by roots
steps.photo_role: Lemna vs Spirodela vs Wolffia macro card
steps.look_for: Lemna = 1 root per frond; Spirodela = several roots per frond; Wolffia = no roots and a minute three-dimensional frond.
steps.why_it_matters: A simple visual character separates the three project duckweed genera.

steps.title: 6 · Taxonomy card: old Lemnaceae → modern Araceae
steps.look_for: Older floras may label Lemna, Spirodela and Wolffia as Lemnaceae; current Kew places them in Araceae.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents conflict between older field keys and the project's current family framework.

steps.title: 7 · Normalize Spirodela spelling
steps.look_for: Source Spirodela polyrrhiza → current accepted spelling Spirodela polyrhiza.
steps.why_it_matters: Avoids creating duplicate concepts from an orthographic variant/source spelling.

comparisons.title: Araceae vs Alismataceae
comparisons.rule: Alismataceae project plants have conspicuous 3-petaled flowers with numerous stamens/carpels and achene heads. Ordinary Araceae packs minute flowers onto a spadix with a spathe; duckweed Araceae is even more reduced.

comparisons.title: Araceae vs Hydrocharitaceae
comparisons.rule: Both include aquatics. Vallisneria has long submerged ribbon leaves and separate floating male/female flower mechanics; duckweed Araceae is free-floating and separated by frond/root architecture, while Pistia forms a floating rosette with a tiny spathe/spadix.

comparisons.title: Duckweeds vs Potamogetonaceae
comparisons.rule: Duckweeds are tiny free-floating fronds with reduced flowers; pondweeds have elongate leafy stems, stipules/prophylls and an emergent flower spike.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not require an obvious spathe/spadix in duckweeds—the duckweed lineage is extremely reduced. Also keep Pistia native/invasive status decisions in the species workflow rather than using family recognition to settle that question.
